title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. The paper reports preregistered design choices, precise execution accounting, representative validator-trace excerpts from the archived artifacts, quantitative analysis, diagnostic interpretation of the ceiling outcome, and artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments required to estimate validator coverage and repair utility.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps workflows with generative models promises efficiency but risks silent or wrong-but-plausible actions unless mechanical checks are deployed before any action is taken. A common mitigation pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a generator (LLM) proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic validator mechanically checks structural and policy constraints, and when necessary a repair module synthesizes corrected candidates or flags human review. Prior work demonstrates GVR-like architectures in code and systems domains and motivates their use in NetOps, yet standardized, preregistered measurements of validator coverage (false-positive/false-negative rates), detection latency, and end-to-end predictive value remain limited [1].

This study (preregistered AC-2026-03) asked whether a multidimensional validator-metric suite explains more variance in end-to-end guarded task success than a single verifier pass rate under paired, shared_initial_candidate semantics. The paired design isolates downstream validator-triggered repair as the only pathway for any difference between baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator+repair permitted) conditions: for each task the generator produced exactly one initial candidate that was reused by both conditions. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The main contribution is an exact, artifact-archived report of a degenerate confirmatory outcome (ceiling) together with artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up confirmatory arms that would produce estimable validator FP/FN and repair utility.
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair and closed-loop verifier architectures have been proposed and evaluated in system and code-generation domains to reduce stochastic generator errors and to provide deterministic acceptance criteria [1]. Benchmarks and task suites for AIOps/NetOps reveal common failure modes—unreliable tickets, false premises, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that complicate end-to-end automation and motivate verifier layers [2],[3]. Prototype systems and design surveys propose self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair to reduce silent or action-triggering failures in tool-augmented LLM systems [4],[5].

These prior records supply architectural motivation and prototype evidence but do not deliver a standardized validator-metric suite tailored for NetOps GVR flows. They therefore motivate the measurement focus of AC-2026-03 without implying empirical coverage guarantees for the deterministic validator used in this run. The present work intentionally treats those prior demonstrations as motivational system reports rather than as establishing empirical validator completeness.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary design. The study was preregistered as AC-2026-03. Key preregistered elements (manifested in the archived preregistration): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json); task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false. The primary confirmatory test was an exact two-sided McNemar test on paired binary success with paired bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistered power plan targeted detection of an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 at α = 0.05 with ~80% power when baseline prevalence permitted variance.

Task bank and deterministic generation. Tasks were drawn deterministically from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1) at difficulty levels labelled 'very_hard' and 'extreme'. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, compact intent, allowed_fields, allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields), and a required_command_sequence. Task selection followed the preregistered deterministic index rule (challenging_workflow_stress_v1). Contamination/exclusion controls (SHA-256 duplicate exclusion and embedding cosine > 0.95 replacement) were preregistered; no exclusions occurred in this execution (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Model and sampling configuration. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini; provider = openai_responses. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 200 and maximum_model_calls = 400. Important artifact-grounded note: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (temperature = null/unset). Null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; provider-side sampling variability may still exist and all provider call audit fields are archived. The adapter recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with the preregistered single shared initial generation per task.

Validator and scoring rule. The deterministic validator used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator implements mechanistic checks and emits per-episode fields: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and repair artifacts when used. The preregistered binary scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) uses validator.valid as the success label for the confirmatory estimand. The pipeline permitted at most one repair call when the validator returned valid = false; any repair call and its trace would be archived under repair_provider_trace fields.

Execution protocol, exclusions, and missingness. The preregistered maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries). The missingness plan mandated complete-pair analysis with a preregistered sensitivity check that treats missing episodes as guarded failures; no missingness or failed episodes occurred (execution manifest: completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0). All raw responses, provider-call traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/execution_log.jsonl, analysis/*) and referenced in the evidence bundle.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter completed the preregistered run: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair). Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. Contamination and exclusion logs are empty (analysis/contamination_summary.csv).

Primary confirmatory outcome. The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0), guarded successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00; exact McNemar two-sided p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. These numeric results are archived and match analysis/artifact records (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Representative validator-trace excerpt (artifact-grounded). The following compact excerpt is verbatim from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json to illustrate validator outputs and why no repairs were requested:

pair_id: pair-000004
normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
parsed_command_count: 4
required_command_count: 4
observed_touched_field_count: 3
valid: true
repair_applied: false
validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
validator_version: 5.0

Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false for every archived episode; repair_applied fields are null throughout the run. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were used, baseline and guarded both evaluated the identical initial candidate for each pair; with validator.valid true for all candidates no downstream repair events occurred and the paired estimator is degenerate.

Exploratory diagnostics. Per-validator FP/FN and repair-latency statistics are uninformative here because no false outcomes or repairs were observed. The execution bundle nevertheless contains full per-episode validator traces and raw responses (execution/raw_results.jsonl) to support reanalysis under alternative scoring or injected-fault conditions. Contamination, missingness, and reconciliation artifacts confirm complete pairing and provider-call accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, analysis/missingness_summary.csv).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the ceiling outcome. The paired shared_initial_candidate design isolates downstream validator-triggered repair as the only source of paired discordance: any difference between baseline and guarded must come from validator-guided repair because the same sampled candidate was reused in both conditions. In this execution three artifact-grounded causes explain the observed ceiling: (1) the synthetic generator produced candidates that satisfied the validator's mechanistic constraints for the recorded generation seeds and generation rules; (2) the single-sample-per-task sampling regime (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1) removed generator variability as a source of disagreements; and (3) the deterministic validator enforces mechanistic checks but does not detect semantic intent misalignment that is correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent. These factors are visible in the archived validator traces (e.g., parsed_command_count == required_command_count and violation_count == 0 across episodes).

Consequences for inferential validity. With baseline success = 1.0 the primary estimand has zero observed variance and the preregistered McNemar test and bootstrap CI are degenerate; the run therefore cannot support inferences about validator benefit under the originally targeted 10-percentage-point improvement. This null-informative outcome is itself an important experimental finding: it identifies a realistic sampling/design risk for paired shared_initial_candidate confirmatory tests and demonstrates the need to preregister perturbations (fault injection) or multi-sample generation to produce estimable baseline error prevalence.

Artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered arms. The archived artifacts and adapter semantics directly support concrete next-step preregistered arms that would create estimable validator metrics without manual artifact fabrication:
1) Deterministic fault-injection arm (preregistered): deterministically inject a catalogued set of faults into reference answers for a controlled fraction f of tasks (syntactic omissions, configuration-logic violations, and semantic-intent swaps). This produces measurable baseline invalidity and allows guarded runs to demonstrate repair benefits. The execution bundle already contains deterministic task replacement and contamination checks to implement this arm reproducibly.
2) Multi-sample stochastic generation: set initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task (with independent sampling seeds recorded). Allow the guarded pipeline to accept any validator-approved draw or to perform repair on rejected draws. This reintroduces generator variability as a potential source of paired discordance and permits estimation of validator FN rates when some draws are invalid by the validator.
3) Multi-validator and multi-model comparison: add an alternative validator implementation and at least one other model family (declared_model_version entries). Comparing validator coverage across implementations and model families quantifies sensitivity to validator design and model sampling.

Threats to validity and limitations. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolates validator-triggered repair but concentrates risk of single-sample ceiling when generator and validator align. Construct validity: the binary validator.valid represents mechanistic correctness (structural/policy checks) but does not capture semantic intent alignment as perceived by human operators. External validity: synthetic task bank, single-model (gpt-5-mini), and single deterministic validator limit generalization to heterogeneous production networks. Conclusion validity: degenerate observed variance in the primary estimand prevents hypothesis testing of the originally targeted effect in this execution. All of these limitations are documented in the execution and analysis artifacts and motivate the prescriptive follow-up arms above.
sections.conclusion: A fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) was executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, the recorded gpt-5-mini shared initial generations, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed the validator's mechanistic checks: no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point improvement) were invalidated by this ceiling outcome. The result is artifact-grounded and reproducible from the archived bundle. The paper publishes the exact execution and analysis artifacts to support replication and proposes concrete, preregistered follow-up arms (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator FP/FN behavior and repair value in operationally meaningful conditions. These follow-up arms are implementable using the same adapter and artifact infrastructure recorded in the execution bundle and are necessary to produce non-degenerate data for estimating validator utility.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
